title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MCP promotes Enterprise-Managed Authorization to stable — one IdP login now governs every connected server
bullets.summary: The Model Context Protocol team moved its Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) extension to stable: orgs centrally control MCP-server access through their IdP and users reach all connected servers via one login. Okta is first (Cross App Access); Asana, Atlassian, Canva, Figma, Granola, Linear, Supabase support it, Slack in progress.
bullets.how: The Construct runs on a fleet of MCP connectors. IdP-governed central auth is the fix for the exact fragility this watchdog catches (connectors silently needing re-auth). Plan a migration so Bobby's connectors renew through one governed login instead of per-server OAuth that breaks scans when it lapses.

bullets.title: The 2026-07-28 MCP spec goes stateless at the protocol layer — 12-month deprecation window opens
bullets.summary: The next MCP version (2026-07-28) makes the protocol stateless with a 12-month window to migrate off legacy versions; adoption is deep (~78% of enterprise AI teams run MCP-backed agents in production, ~97M monthly SDK downloads).
bullets.how: A stateless protocol layer is friendly to our failure mode: scheduled scans dying when a session/host closes. Pin the version the Construct agents speak, schedule the migration before the legacy window bites, and treat the runtime spec as a governed dependency.

bullets.title: OpenAI clears Commerce review for a broad GPT-5.6 launch this week — Sol / Terra / Luna + Ultra mode
bullets.summary: GPT-5.6 ships as three tiers — Sol (frontier), Terra (~5.5-level intelligence at roughly half the cost), Luna (small/fast) — plus an Ultra mode with a Max reasoning level and heavier sub-agent use; Commerce green-lit a wide release expected this week.
bullets.how: Routing-layer input, not a rebuild. Terra's '5.5-level at half cost' is worth benching against Sonnet 5 and Haiku for fan-out/verify tiers where we split cheap vs. hardest work. Keep routing provider-agnostic; don't re-architect around a just-GA'd model.

bullets.title: Anthropic opens Claude for Government (Code + Cowork, FedRAMP High) as Cowork mobile/web beta keeps rolling
bullets.summary: Claude launched a public beta of Claude Code and Cowork inside Claude for Government Desktop (FedRAMP High, tamper-evident audit logs, spend governance), while consumer Cowork mobile/web keeps rolling out on paid plans (Max first).
bullets.how: (a) FedRAMP-High Cowork is a credible public-sector wedge for Construct/B9 gov-adjacent SMB work; (b) as execution moves cross-device, re-confirm our scheduled scans survive it — this watchdog is the standing test.

bullets.title: The 2026 SMB-agent verdict: integration depth wins, and 'personal AI marketing team' is now a named category
bullets.summary: Round-ups converge that agents connecting directly into Shopify, HubSpot, Stripe, calendars, email and shipping beat isolated tools, with SMBs reportedly cutting opex 35–45% within 90 days; competitors (e.g. NoimosAI) position as a 'unified squad of agents' handling strategy, SEO, social and GEO.
bullets.how: This is Brand 9 Signs' own thesis sold back to the market. The moat is integration depth + owned-presence/GEO — exactly Pulse's stack. Sharpen B9 positioning against the 'AI marketing team' framing and make connector depth (GBP, social, WP/Yoast, reviews) the visible proof.

praxis_lesson: Two of today's five items (MCP EMA going stable, the stateless 2026-07-28 spec) point at the same fix for the fragility that makes this watchdog necessary: auth and protocol state are moving from per-server, session-bound, silently-breakable plumbing to centralized, governed, stateless infrastructure. Get ahead of it — adopt IdP-governed connector auth, pin and schedule the MCP version migration, and keep treating the agent runtime (models, connectors, protocol) as a monitored, patchable dependency rather than fire-and-forget wiring.
